judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not mention or challenge the claim about Baes2020a regarding 'convergence criterion for numerical Abel-transform inversions in triaxial stellar systems.' No flag corresponds to this injected mis-attribution.

The review discusses triaxiality and non-spherical geometries in general, but it does not mention Baes2020a or challenge any claim about what that specific cited source established. Under the broadened-claim citation rule, this is not a specific source-claim contradiction.

The reviewer mentions triaxiality only in the context of the author's defense of spherical symmetry and does not challenge the fabricated claim regarding Baes 2020a or Abel-transform convergence criteria.

The reviewer does not challenge or flag the claim about Baes (2020) establishing 'convergence criteria for numerical Abel-transform inversions in triaxial stellar systems.' The reviewer's comment 4 on non-spherical geometries is about the paper's own assumptions, not about mischaracterizing what Baes 2020 showed. No specific flag targets the injected misattribution.
The reviewer makes no mention of any discrepancy between the Figure 1 caption value (γ=0.24) and the body text value (γ=0.25). There is no flag related to this numerical inconsistency.
The reviewer does not mention Figure 1's caption value, the inner slope gamma being 0.24 versus 0.25, or any caption-body inconsistency. No specific numeric mismatch is flagged.
The reviewer does not mention the value of the inner slope gamma or any inconsistency between the figure captions and the body text.
The reviewer does not flag any issue with the sign in the sharp-transition limit equation, nor does it mention any inconsistency in the normalization exponent in Section 2's equations.
There is no comment about a sign error, the sharp-transition limit equation, continuity at R=Rb, or inconsistency with Eq. (coreSersic). The mathematics injection was not specifically identified.

The reviewer praises the conclusions without flagging the overstated generalization about admissibility constraints governing 'any parametric photometric model applied across the full spectrum of galaxy types and environments.' No such critique appears in the report.

The reviewer is generally positive about the paper's scope and does not flag the conclusion as overgeneralized to all parametric photometric models or all galaxy types and environments. No specific objection corresponds to the injected sweeping concluding clause.
The reviewer does not challenge the broad claim in the conclusion, instead describing the paper as clearly written and impactful without addressing the scope expansion.
